subject.title: [Feature]: Browser tool: snapshot-on-navigate and fewer round-trips/setup dead-ends

question: Should successful browser navigation always include a compact snapshot, and should browser availability be hidden from the model rather than exposed with actionable runtime errors?
rationale: Both choices change the browser tool’s model-facing contract, token cost, and recovery behavior; source-level mechanics alone cannot determine the preferred product policy.

options.title: Split and sponsor snapshot-on-navigate
options.body: Land a narrowly specified browser-plugin change for compact post-navigation snapshots, while tracking gating, remediation, and lifecycle behavior separately.

options.title: Keep explicit snapshots
options.body: Retain the existing two-action model loop and address only targeted runtime diagnostics or lifecycle defects if independently confirmed.

options.title: Adopt a gated browser contract
options.body: Define a reliable provisioned/unavailable capability contract before hiding the tool or changing failure exposure.

recommendation.title: Split and sponsor snapshot-on-navigate
recommendation.body: Land a narrowly specified browser-plugin change for compact post-navigation snapshots, while tracking gating, remediation, and lifecycle behavior separately.

likelyOwner.reason: The available context establishes the author as the only identified participant with concrete browser-tool problem analysis; code-history ownership could not be established here.
